title: Espinacas con Garbanzos
subtitle: Sevillian spinach and chickpea stew with cumin and smoked paprika
excerpt: Espinacas con garbanzos is the most famous dish of Seville: wilted spinach and chickpeas cooked with garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and a thick slice of bread fried and blended into the sauce to thicken it. It is served in every tapas bar in Seville as both a side dish and a main. The bread-thickened sauce is distinctive and delicious.
sourceNotes: Espinacas con garbanzos is a signature dish of Seville and Andalusian cooking. The combination of spinach and chickpeas with cumin and paprika reflects the Moorish culinary tradition that shaped Andalusian cooking. The bread fried in oil and blended into the sauce is a technique called majado -- a paste used to thicken and flavour stews across Spain.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made several hours ahead. Reheat gently.

content.text: The key step is the majado: a thick slice of bread is fried in olive oil until golden, then blended with a little water into a paste and stirred into the stew. This thickens the sauce and gives it a rich, slightly bready quality that is completely different from a flour-thickened sauce. Do not skip this step.

items.prepNote: defrosted and squeezed dry, or 700g fresh spinach wilted and squeezed

content.text: Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a large pan over medium heat. Fry {{bread-white}} bread slices until golden on both sides, about 2 minutes. Remove, break into pieces, blend with 4 tablespoons of water until smooth. Set aside.
In the same pan, add {{onion}} onion and cook for 8 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add {{smoked-paprika}} smoked paprika and {{cumin-ground}} cumin and stir for 30 seconds.

Add {{spinach-frozen}} spinach, {{chickpeas-tinned}} chickpeas, and the bread paste. Add 200 ml of water and {{salt-table}} salt. Stir to combine. Simmer for 10 minutes until everything is well coated and the sauce is thick. Add {{sherry-vinegar}} sherry vinegar. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with crusty bread.

items.symptom: The stew is dry and the chickpeas are sticking
items.cause: Not enough liquid was added, or it reduced too fast.
items.fix: Add water a splash at a time and stir. The stew should be thick but not dry -- it should coat the chickpeas without being runny.

content.text: Espinacas con garbanzos is the most famous dish of Seville. It appears on every tapas menu and in every home kitchen in the city. The dish reflects Andalusia's Moorish heritage: the combination of cumin, paprika, and chickpeas with leafy greens comes from the Arab cooking that dominated southern Spain for 700 years. It is one of the great vegetarian dishes of Spanish cooking, though it is rarely thought of that way -- it is just everyday Sevillian food.
